from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Convolution is a sliding window operator.",
            "Imagine a 3x3 filter passing over pixels.",
            "Multiply pixel values by filter weights.",
            "Sum results to produce new pixel value.",
            "This process smooths digital images."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Intuitive Hook: The 'Moving Window' Concept", lecture_lines)
        
        # 1. Display a 5x5 grid of pixels
        pixels = VGroup()
        for i in range(5):
            for j in range(5):
                pixel = Square(side_length=0.7, stroke_width=2, color=WHITE)
                pixel.move_to(self.grid['B2'] + np.array([j*0.75, -i*0.75, 0]))
                pixels.add(pixel)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(pixels))
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FF5733")

        # 2. Create 3x3 window square outline
        window = Square(side_length=2.25, stroke_width=4, color="#FF0000")
        window.move_to(pixels[0:3].get_center() + pixels[5:8].get_center() + pixels[10:13].get_center() / 3)
        window.move_to(pixels.get_center())

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(Create(window))
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#33FF57")

        # 3. Multiply pixel values (highlight window pixels)
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(Indicate(window, color="#FF0000", scale_factor=1.05))
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#3357FF")

        # 4. Sum results (moving the window)
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        # Move the window across the grid
        self.play(window.animate.shift(LEFT * 0.75), run_time=1)
        self.play(window.animate.shift(UP * 0.75), run_time=1)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[3].set_color("#F333FF")

        # 5. This process smooths images
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.play(Flash(window.get_center(), color="#FFFFFF", line_length=0.2))
        self.lecture[3].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[4].set_color("#FFD700")
        self.wait(1)

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "The discrete formula defines convolution.",
            "Flip the kernel before sliding.",
            "Weights determine the output transformation.",
            "Sliding across input produces output sequence.",
            "Moving average simplifies 1D data."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Mathematical Mechanics", lecture_lines)
        
        # Elements
        input_data = [1, 2, 3]
        kernel_data = [0.5, 0.5]

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===

        self.play(FadeIn(input_mobj), FadeIn(kernel_mobj))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        self.play(kernel_mobj.animate.rotate(PI))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===

        self.place_at_grid(output_cell, 'D2')
        self.play(FadeIn(output_cell))

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Application: Feature Detection", ["Kernels act as pattern detectors.", "Positive and negative values identify edges.", "High contrast yields strong signal response."])
        
        # Reveal lecture lines sequentially
        self.play(FadeIn(self.lecture[0]))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1: Kernels act as pattern detectors ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(BLUE)
        img = Square(side_length=2, color=WHITE, fill_opacity=0.3)
        self.place_in_area(img, 'A1', 'C3')
        self.play(Create(img))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2: Positive and negative values identify edges ===
        self.play(FadeIn(self.lecture[1]))
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        kernel = Matrix([[-1, 0, 1], [-1, 0, 1], [-1, 0, 1]], v_buff=0.3, h_buff=0.3).set_color(YELLOW)
        self.place_at_grid(kernel, 'B5', scale_factor=0.5)
        self.play(FadeIn(kernel))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3: High contrast yields strong signal response ===
        self.play(FadeIn(self.lecture[2]))
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(GREEN)
        
        edge_detection = Line(start=ORIGIN, end=UP*1.5, color=GREEN, stroke_width=6)
        self.place_at_grid(edge_detection, 'E4')
        self.play(Create(edge_detection))
        
        self.wait(2)

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Summary & Synthesis", ["Step one: Choose a kernel.", "Step two: Slide, multiply, and sum.", "Step three: Analyze the resulting map."])
        
        # Define terms
        window = Text("Window", color=BLUE)
        kernel = Text("Kernel", color=GREEN)
        feature_map = Text("Feature Map", color=YELLOW)

        self.place_at_grid(feature_map, "E4")
        
        # Arrows
        arrow1 = Arrow(start=window.get_right(), end=kernel.get_left(), color=WHITE)
        arrow2 = Arrow(start=kernel.get_bottom(), end=feature_map.get_top(), color=WHITE)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(Write(window), Write(kernel), Write(arrow1))
        self.lecture[0].set_color(BLUE)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(Write(arrow2))
        self.lecture[1].set_color(GREEN)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(Write(feature_map))
        self.lecture[2].set_color(YELLOW)

outline.topic: Discrete Convolutions: From Image Blurring to Feature Detection

sections.title: Intuitive Hook: The 'Moving Window' Concept
sections.content: Define convolution as a sliding window operator. Before introducing the math, visualize a small 'filter' (kernel) passing over a 2D grid of values (pixels). Explain that at each position, we perform an element-wise multiplication and summation.
sections.example: Imagine a 3x3 'blurring lens' hovering over a digital photo of a cat, averaging the pixels beneath it to smooth out noise.

sections.title: Mathematical Mechanics (Graphical Representation)
sections.content: Transition to the formal discrete formula: (f * g)[n] = Σ f[k]g[n-k]. Use a visual animation where the kernel is 'flipped' and slid across the signal. Highlight the importance of the kernel's values (weights) in determining the output transformation.
sections.example: Represent a 1D sequence [1, 2, 3] being convolved with a filter [0.5, 0.5] to create a simple moving average graph.

sections.title: Application: Feature Detection in Computer Vision
sections.content: Explain how different kernels act as 'detectors.' A kernel with positive values on one side and negative on the other will produce high outputs where brightness changes abruptly—effectively identifying edges.
sections.example: An animation showing a Sobel filter detecting the outline of a robot's chassis by highlighting high-contrast gradients.

sections.title: Real-World Integration: Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs)
sections.content: Synthesize the knowledge. Explain that in modern AI, the computer 'learns' the optimal filter weights to identify complex objects. This is the foundation of image recognition in autonomous vehicles.
sections.example: A diagram showing a smart vacuum cleaner 'seeing' a dog vs. a slipper by passing a series of learned convolution layers over the sensor data.

sections.title: Summary & Synthesis
sections.content: Recap the three core steps: 1. Choose a kernel, 2. Slide/Multiply/Sum, 3. Analyze the output. Emphasize that convolution is the mathematical 'language' of spatial pattern recognition.
sections.example: A quick visual 'speed-run' showing the transformation of raw pixels into a simplified 'Edge Map' and then into a high-level label: 'Object Detected: Shiba Inu'.
